positions.as_written: Follow up in the survival studies is long, which is a genuine strength, and the cohorts are from eras with different indications and techniques, which limits what the survival figures transfer to.
Read correction targets with the radiographic protocol and the laxity assessment attached.
Treat survival series as evidence about selected patients and techniques of their era.
Read the dynamic alignment work before planning in a knee with a thrust, since the static film will mislead.
Do not quote the mechanical argument as though it were the clinical evidence.
Weigh age and physiology, since this operation's whole case is that it buys time a younger patient needs.
Weigh comorbidities, because union and rehabilitation both depend on them and smoking in particular changes the arithmetic.
Weigh the demands on the knee, since osteotomy suits a patient who intends to keep loading the joint hard and arthroplasty does not.
Weigh their psychological state and their tolerance of a long recovery, because this is the operation patients most often abandon partway through rehabilitation.
State the balance, and record what the alternative was and why it was not chosen.
Read the long survival series for what they say about correction and the short trials for what they say about symptoms, and do not merge them.
